subject.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)

question: Should this PR keep runtime invalidation for legacy no-code, no-pluginId missing-source diagnostics, or require a narrower legacy path before merge?
rationale: Persisted registry behavior is upgrade-sensitive, and the predecessor maintainer decision rejected no-pluginId as an orphan signal without a more explicit owner/kind; the remaining choice is a compatibility tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical review point.

options.title: Require Narrow Legacy Proof
options.body: Keep the explicit marker/schema fix, but require redacted latest-head legacy-upgrade output and either a narrower legacy guard or maintainer acceptance before merge.

options.title: Accept Runtime Legacy Invalidation
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the runtime rederive tradeoff for all no-code, no-pluginId missing-source legacy diagnostics after deciding the startup unblock is worth the compatibility cost.

options.title: Move Legacy Cleanup To Doctor
options.body: Remove the runtime no-code fallback and handle old SQLite rows through doctor, refresh, or migration-owned cleanup instead.

recommendation.title: Require Narrow Legacy Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the explicit marker/schema fix, but require redacted latest-head legacy-upgrade output and either a narrower legacy guard or maintainer acceptance before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc gave the explicit predecessor direction that defines the remaining compatibility choice.
